extracted.intended_audience: students and general readers interested in American party politics
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying normative and descriptive criteria about the composition, behaviour, and evolution of American political parties as presented in a political science/textbook chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to federal vs. state power contingent on political position
rubrics_metrics.description: A party's devotion to the principle of Federal power has been but slightly tested and 'their action in a concrete case would probably depend on whether their party was at the time in condition to use that power for its own purposes.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a party is in minority in Congress it 'would be little inclined to strengthen Congress against the States.' Use this as a heuristic: party constitutional principles are applied opportunistically according to political advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electoral calculus drives stance on liquor regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: On the regulation or extinction of the liquor traffic 'the point of consequence is what they can gain or lose.' Parties avoid firm commitments because of the ethnic and electoral consequences (Irish, Germans, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine how constituency composition (e.g., immigrant groups, temperance supporters) shapes party rhetoric and policy positions; parties may use 'flattering phrases' to conciliate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguity or non-commitment on tariff to avoid alienating regions
rubrics_metrics.description: Though Democrats historically favoured tariff for revenue, 'the party... is practically divided upon the tariff issue' and parties have 'sought to remain unpledged' to avoid alienating districts with opposing economic interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret formal declarations cautiously; parties often adopt ambiguous or flexible positions to reconcile regional economic interests (iron, sugar, timber producers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil service reform often receives lip service; real change driven externally
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil service reform 'long received the lip service of both parties' and changes effected were 'either forced on the parties by public opinion... or... due to the enlightened views of individual Presidents.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess party commitment to administrative reform by looking for whether reforms are leader-driven or imposed by public pressure rather than purely party initiative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation of corporate abuses seen as bipartisan duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Both parties have asserted 'it is the duty of railways to serve the people' and measures like the Interstate Commerce Act 'cannot be called a party measure.' Both profess eagerness to 'restrain the abuse of their powers by corporations, and to put an end to monopolies.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat certain regulatory initiatives (railroads, monopolies) as non-partisan or broadly supported across parties; evaluate policy as public-interest rather than strict party doctrine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive economic policies (e.g., currency) can cause schisms
rubrics_metrics.description: In 1896 Democrats pledged to free coinage of silver leading to a secession of an important section; such issues can produce schism though the reunited party may lack a distinctive currency policy afterward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use presence or absence of clear economic doctrine as an indicator of party cohesion and potential for factional splits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties may defer contentious territorial/imperial policy
rubrics_metrics.description: On questions like the Philippines 'there cannot be said to be to-day any controversy between [the parties]' and such questions are 'admitted to be one for the future, not for the present.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where parties treat an issue as for future debate, expect short-term strategic convergence and postponement of doctrinal division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pragmatism on state-level social reforms
rubrics_metrics.description: On matters belonging to State politics (woman suffrage, ballot reform, child labour, eight-hour law, convict labour) 'Neither party has any distinctive attitude... each will advocate it when there seems a practically useful object to be secured, or when the popular voice seems to call for it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate party positions on social reforms as pragmatic and responsive to popular demands rather than as fixed ideological commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition as temporary strategy rather than settled doctrine
rubrics_metrics.description: A party opposing the President 'may at any given moment seek to damage him by defeating some particular proposal he has made... but this it will do as a piece of temporary strategy, not in pursuance of any settled doctrine.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish tactical opposition from principled doctrinal disagreement when analyzing inter-party conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive 'spirit' or sentiment between parties
rubrics_metrics.description: There is 'a difference of spirit or sentiment' between the two great parties, a contrast perceptible in tone and temper beyond formal policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider cultural, temperamental, and social dispositions of party supporters as part of party identity in addition to policy positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Party organizations can retard natural political evolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Party organizations are 'strong things, and often interfere with the course of natural evolution,' slowing reconstruction or realignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for organizational inertia when assessing the pace and likelihood of party realignment or emergence of new parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of a great party: adapt and devise new doctrines
rubrics_metrics.description: The duty of a great party is 'to face these, to find answers and remedies, applying to the facts of the hour the doctrines it has lived by... and, when they have ceased to be applicable, thinking out new doctrines conformable to the main principles and tendencies which it represents.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge party quality by its capacity to innovate doctrinally and to formulate practical remedies for new problems; leadership must diffuse conclusions through followers.

rubrics_metrics.name: American parties change slower due to strong organizations and mass conciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Change happens more slowly in America 'partly due to the completeness and strength of the party organizations' and 'partly to the growing prominence of social and labour' questions both parties seek to conciliate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare institutional and social factors across systems when predicting speed of party transformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate parties by social, local, racial and ecclesiastical complexions
rubrics_metrics.description: It is desirable 'to convey some idea of what may be called their social and local, their racial and ecclesiastical complexions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include demographic, geographic, ethnic, and religious composition as primary axes when analyzing party character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Party strength derives from coalition composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Republican party 'brought to the new party solidity, political experience, and a large number of wealthy and influential adherents' plus 'force and enthusiasm' from abolitionists — coalition components shape party capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess which social/economic elements (wealthy elites, moral reformers, veterans) form the party coalition to explain its resilience and public image.

rubrics_metrics.name: Socioeconomic and regional bases of party support
rubrics_metrics.description: In the North: 'merchants, manufacturers, and professional men... tend to be Republicans'; farmers in the Mississippi valley; working class divided but 'the more solid part... are generally Republicans'; regional patterns change toward the South where 'very few men of good standing belong to the Republican party.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map parties onto class, occupational, and regional groups; use local social composition to predict party dominance in areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional social acceptability affects party membership
rubrics_metrics.description: In the South it is 'not easy for an educated man to remain a Republican' because social milieu favors Democrats; party managers are 'apt to be black sheep.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factor social stigma and local elite networks into explanations for regional party weakness or strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Swing states decided by circumstances, local causes, candidate merits
rubrics_metrics.description: In Middle States (New York, New Jersey, Ohio, Indiana) parties are nearly balanced and 'the majority of votes is seen to sway now this way now that, as the circumstances of the hour, or local causes, or the merits of individual candidates, may affect the popular mind.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat electoral outcomes in balanced states as contingent and sensitive to short-term factors rather than deep-seated partisanship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factional tendencies can cause temporary desertion or bolting
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections of Republicans 'explained their conduct by declaring that the great claims... had been forfeited by mal-administration... If intelligence and cultivation dispose their possessors to desert... the party would have been stronger without this element' and some sections 'bolt' though many are reabsorbed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze internal dissent and factionalism as sources of temporary weakness; track whether splinter groups are reabsorbed or lead to lasting splits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical reputation and administrative performance shape party fortunes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Democratic party 'was long discredited by its sympathy with the South' and later profited from being in opposition; when in power its legislation 'was not higher in aim... than that which Republican congresses have produced.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reputation from past positions and the quality of governance while in office to evaluate a party's electoral prospects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Urban immigrant bases shape party image and support
rubrics_metrics.description: The Democratic party's strength in cities derives from 'a vast ignorant fluctuating mass... many of them recently admitted to citizenship' attracted to the party by name or leaders of their own races; this 'gives the party a slight flavour of rowdyism.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how immigrant composition and urban machine politics affect party reputation and mobilization capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethnic groups' partisan alignment is historically contingent and may decay
rubrics_metrics.description: Race differences and nationality groups (Irish, Germans, Scandinavians, French Canadians) 'have played a considerable part' but their political identities diminish over generations; e.g., Germans estimated 'five-ninths Republican, four-ninths Democratic' and cohesion declines in twentieth century.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect ethnic voting patterns to weaken over generations; analyze initial causes (religion, temperance, slavery stance) for alignment and track assimilation effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irish cohesion and linkage to Democrats due to religion and urban politics
rubrics_metrics.description: The Irish 'have retained their national spirit and disposition to act together' and were 'for a good while nearly all Democrats' due to religion and early urban power; though later many Irish joined Republicans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study organizational leadership and ethnic solidarity to explain durable party alignment, and note conditions under which realignment occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural practices (e.g., alcohol) and religion influence alignment (Germans)
rubrics_metrics.description: Germans were often Republican because of hostility to slavery and because the 'German colonist is faithful to the beer of his fatherland'—Republican hostility to liquor pushed some Germans toward Democrats in cities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include cultural preferences and religious affiliations as predictors of party preference, especially where policy positions (temperance) affect group interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enfranchisement and organization determine political influence of Negroes
rubrics_metrics.description: Negroes in the North are 'mostly Republicans' out of gratitude, but in the South 'seven Southern States have so altered their constitutions as to exclude nine-tenths of the negroes from the suffrage.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the practical political power of racial groups by measuring enfranchisement, access to organization, and barriers to participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religion plays limited direct role unless institutional influence is perceived
rubrics_metrics.description: Religion 'comes very little into American party except when... the advance of the Roman Catholic Church and the idea that she exerts her influence to secure...' (sentence continues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat religion as a latent factor that becomes salient when organized religious institutions are perceived to exert political influence; otherwise its role is muted.
